1. Identifies core contact center infrastructure entities on the whiteboard: Amazon Connect, AWS Lambda (top IVR logic), Amazon ECS microservices, external CRMs (Salesforce/Siebel), Amazon SES, AWS Lambda (bottom email logic), Amazon DynamoDB, Agent Browser, ContactSuite platform (comprising ELB, EC2, ASG, SenseIQ Knowledge Base), and Amazon RDS.
2. Prunes generic human actors (Caller Carrie, Agent Andy) per Rule 5, retaining system entry points and client interfaces (Amazon Connect, Amazon SES, Agent Browser).
3. Normalizes all service types to strict AWS and Client vocabulary (Connect, Lambda, ECS, ThirdParty, SES, DynamoDB, EC2, RDS).
4. Establishes flows: Flow 0 for inbound call/chat processing via Connect, Lambda, ECS, and CRMs; Flow 1 for incoming email processing via SES, Lambda, and DynamoDB; Flow 2 for agent browser interaction with ContactSuite; Flow 3 for reporting data persistence from ContactSuite to RDS.

graph.name: ContactSuite Amazon Connect Architecture
graph.notes: ContactSuite provides contact center scaling, integrating voice, chat, and email with Amazon Connect, AWS Lambda, ECS, SES, DynamoDB, and RDS.

nodes.name: Amazon Connect
nodes.notes: Handles inbound chat and voice channels.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (IVR)
nodes.notes: Executes IVR logic based on contact flows and caller inputs.

nodes.name: Amazon ECS
nodes.notes: Runs containerized microservices for external integration.

nodes.name: External CRMs
nodes.notes: Third-party customer relationship management tools like Salesforce or Siebel.

nodes.name: Amazon DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores email interaction states and data.

nodes.name: Agent Browser
nodes.notes: Web browser interface used by contact center agents authenticated via 2FA.

nodes.name: ContactSuite Platform
nodes.notes: Core platform container hosted on ELB, EC2, and ASG including SenseIQ Knowledge Base.

nodes.name: Amazon RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database used for reporting and historical KPI persistence.

edges.notes: Amazon Connect invokes Lambda to execute IVR contact flow logic.
Lambda triggers ECS microservices for downstream backend operations.
ECS microservices connect out to external CRMs like Salesforce or Siebel.
Amazon SES forwards incoming email events to AWS Lambda.
Lambda saves processed email information into Amazon DynamoDB.
Agent browser connects into the ContactSuite platform with 2FA.
ContactSuite persists reporting and operational analytics to Amazon RDS.
